column1: Pioneers of Soviet Computing|1995|10|0|1991|7.5,8,7,7.5,6.5,8.5,10,8.5,5.5,6|Boris N. Malinovsky|Historical explanation and participant memoir of computing projects, not a technical curriculum. Hardware supply, military patronage and bureaucratic constraints are transferable. Source review finds valuable primary material but disordered chronology and too little software context; D=6.5 reflects this mixed yield rather than a penalty for technical detail. Soviet focus warrants T11. Original Russian 1995, English available: https://w.icfcst.kiev.ua/MUSEUM/MALINOVSKY/books_e.html . End 1991 approximate for the central Soviet period; later diary material is ancillary.

Mathematical People|1985|0|0|1985|7.5,5.5,6.5,5,7,8.5,8,8.5,7,7|Donald J. Albers and Gerald L. Alexanderson|Interviews and profiles of mathematicians qualify under the science-biography exception, without technical training as primary purpose. Research careers and institutional conditions add intellectual context. Source comments and catalog description support D=7 provisionally; variable interview yield and limited systematic causal analysis restrain M. https://books.google.com/books?id=s-fXAAAAMAAJ verifies original 1985 and authors. Endpoint 1985 is approximate for original collection.

Fascinating Mathematical People|2011|0|0|2010|7.5,4.5,5,4.5,5.5,8,8,8.5,6.5,7|Donald J. Albers and Gerald L. Alexanderson|Science-biography exception applies. Gwern reports uneven interviews, limited explanation of work, and several useful career episodes; the mathematical association review is more favorable. D=5.5 is a low-confidence whole-book estimate, not an acceptance of either review as objective measurement. https://old.maa.org/node/112018 and https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctt7sc69 . Original 2011; endpoint 2010 approximate. No technical-course exclusion.

The Lady Tasting Tea|2001|0|0|2000|7.5,7,6.5,6.5,6.5,8.5,9,8,6.5,7|David Salsburg|Narrative history of statistical discoveries and industrial quality applications, not a methods course. The source reader finds the blend of biography and explanation unfocused; catalog description confirms a range of cases. D=6.5 and N=6.5 reflect separate concerns: uneven learning per chapter and organization. https://search.worldcat.org/title/1022680066 confirms 2001, correcting the source's 2002 edition date. End 2000 approximate for twentieth-century coverage.

Drift into Failure|2011|0|0||6,8,7,7,5.5,8,9,8.5,6.5,6|Sidney Dekker|Sustained explanation of organizational failure, not a procedural safety manual. Source review gives specific concerns about caricatured reductionism, repetitive complexity claims and weak treatment of improving safety; these lower E and D for distinct reasons. One hostile reader report is insufficient to establish a serious central V1 failure, so retain with low confidence. https://catalog.libraries.vsc.edu/cgi-bin/koha/opac-ISBDdetail.pl?biblionumber=344203 confirms 2011 and contents. Cross-case theory has no single endpoint.

Spam Nation|2014|0|0|2014|8,8,7.5,8,7.5,7.5,9,8.5,6,6|Brian Krebs|Explains cybercrime through hosting, payment networks, affiliate incentives and leaked organizational records. Source reader reports unusual access and useful detail, with weak organization and inflated rhetoric; these chiefly lower N/P, while D=7.5 reflects substantive distinct cases. Computing economics is central, not warfare or partisan politics. https://books.google.com/books?id=81_WngEACAAJ confirms original 2014. Historical endpoint 2014 approximate; operational specifics age faster than the incentives.
